title: Energy and Work Done
seo_title: Secondary 2 Science: Energy and Work Done Worksheets (Lower Secondary Science with Answers)
standard_code: Secondary 2: Application of Forces and Transfer of Energy (Energy and work done)
standard_text: State the joule as the SI unit of work and energy; identify work done as the energy transferred when an object moves in the direction of a force; infer that energy can be converted from one form to another and is conserved; show curiosity about the impact of using different energy sources (summary of the MOE Lower Secondary Science Syllabus).
meta_desc: Free Secondary 2 science worksheets for Singapore students on energy: forms of energy, energy conversion, conservation of energy, work done = force × distance and energy sources. With answers.
key_big: Energy is converted, never created or destroyed.
body_html:
How to think about it

Energy cannot be created or destroyed. It is converted from one form to another.

  • Forms: kinetic, gravitational potential, elastic potential, chemical potential, thermal, light, sound, electrical, nuclear.
  • Energy and work are measured in joules (J).
  • Work done = force × distance moved in the direction of the force. No movement, no work.
  • Renewable sources (solar, wind, hydroelectric) will not run out; fossil fuels (coal, oil, natural gas) will.
Example

A 40 N force pushes a trolley 5 m. Work done?

40 × 5

Answer: 200 J

Example

Energy change in a torch?

battery → bulb

Answer: chemical potential → electrical → light and thermal

Common mistakes

  • Saying energy is 'used up'. It is converted, often to thermal energy.
  • Thinking holding something still is doing work. Nothing moves, so no work is done.
  • Dividing force by distance. Work done = force × distance.
  • Calling solar energy non-renewable.

faq.a: No. Energy is converted to other forms, often thermal energy that spreads to the surroundings.
When a force moves an object in the direction of the force. Work done = force × distance.
